verdicts.description: [LLM-Judge] Two distinct Unicode subjects (Turkish dotted/dotless I) were normalized/collapsed into the same identity entity, enabling account/identity confusion.

sequences.description: Attempt to use a JWT minted for audience 'svc-A' to authenticate against a role bound to audience 'svc-B' (role confusion / audience bypass). Includes a control login that should succeed.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: A JWT must not be accepted by a role whose bound_audiences do not include the token's aud; otherwise effective permissions exceed the upstream intent for that audience.

params.description: jwt auth for I5 audience mismatch tests

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control login failed or could not read svc-a secret; setup invalid or policy binding broken
Role bound to svc-B accepted JWT with aud=svc-A, indicating missing audience binding
Audience-mismatched login gained access to svc-b protected resource

sequences.description: Test numeric claim coercion: role expects integer department_id=100, attacker presents float 100.7. If coerced/truncated to match, attacker may receive permissions beyond upstream intent. Includes a control login with exact integer.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: Claim constraints must be enforced without unsafe numeric coercion; a float value must not satisfy an integer-bound claim if it changes authorization outcome.

params.description: jwt auth for I5 numeric coercion tests

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control login with department_id=100 failed; cannot interpret numeric coercion results
Float department_id=100.7 satisfied integer-bound claim department_id=100, enabling unauthorized policy grant
Attacker with float department_id read dept100 secret, indicating unsafe claim coercion or constraint bypass

sequences.description: Attempt group-policy escalation: role grants only low-priv policy, but attacker supplies groups claim that maps (via external group alias) to an admin policy group. Verify attacker cannot read admin secret.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: Effective permissions must not exceed role/broker policy; upstream group claims must not allow escalation beyond intended grants for the auth context.

params.description: jwt auth for I5 group escalation tests

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control user without admins group could read admin secret; baseline authorization binding is broken
Attacker escalated to admin secret access via groups claim mapping, exceeding role/broker policy intent

sequences.description: Attack empty_bound_claims: role uses bound_claims={} (no effective constraint) but grants privileged policy; verify that a non-intended principal can still obtain admin access (should be rejected by policy intent).
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: A role intended to restrict privileged access via claim constraints must not grant admin permissions when bound_claims is empty (no constraint). If empty bound_claims results in unconstrained access, EffectivePerms exceeds BrokerPolicy intent.

params.description: jwt mount for I5 tests

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control admin principal could not read admin secret; setup invalid or policy not applied
Role with empty claim constraints granted admin access to a non-admin principal (authorization binding violated)

sequences.description: Attack default_role confusion: mount default_role initially points to low-priv role; after admin changes default_role to high-priv role, attacker omits role in login and attempts to gain elevated access unexpectedly.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: Omitting role should not allow privilege escalation via default_role changes; effective permissions must remain within intended broker policy for the authentication context.

params.description: jwt mount for default_role tests

oracle_checks.violation_description: Attacker obtained admin access before default_role change; baseline authorization binding failed
Changing mount default_role caused attacker (tier=user) to gain admin access when omitting role (authorization binding violated)

sequences.description: empty_audience: Role is configured with bound_audiences=[] (deny-all intent). Test whether Vault incorrectly treats empty list as unconstrained and issues a token with privileged policy.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: A role with an empty bound_audiences list must not authorize JWTs with an aud claim; otherwise effective permissions exceed broker policy intent (audience binding bypass).

params.description: jwt mount for empty audience bypass test

oracle_checks.violation_description: Role with bound_audiences=[] should reject JWTs with aud, but login succeeded (audience binding bypass).
Attacker should not be able to read admin secret if audience binding is enforced; read succeeded implies over-grant.

verdicts.description: [LLM-Judge] JWT role configured with bound_audiences=[] (deny-all intent) still allowed successful logins and issued tokens (albeit only with default policy).

sequences.description: Config-change + re-auth: Start with permissive role granting admin policy, then tighten role to remove admin policy. Re-login with same upstream principal and verify new token cannot access admin secret (no policy stickiness across re-auth).
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: After role policy tightening, a new login must not receive permissions beyond the updated broker policy; otherwise authorization binding is violated across config changes.

params.description: jwt mount for role tighten test

oracle_checks.violation_description: After role tightening, a new login still accessed admin secret, indicating permissions exceeded updated broker policy.
After tightening, user should still retain intended minimal access; failure suggests misbinding or unintended denial (test sanity).

sequences.description: Issuer substitution: Configure bound_issuer and a role granting privileged policy. Attempt login with mismatched iss but otherwise valid claims. If accepted, broker policy (issuer binding) is bypassed and permissions exceed intent.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: Effective permissions must be bounded by broker policy including issuer binding; a JWT with iss != bound_issuer must be rejected and must not yield privileged access.

params.description: jwt mount for issuer substitution test

oracle_checks.violation_description: JWT with iss != bound_issuer should be rejected; acceptance indicates issuer binding bypass leading to over-grant.
Even if login succeeds unexpectedly, token must not grant admin secret access; access indicates authorization binding failure.
Control token with correct issuer should be able to read admin secret; failure indicates broken setup rather than a security property.

sequences.description: Attack: Misconfigure identity_claim_json_pointer so identity is derived from a nested claim that attacker can set to a privileged alias value, potentially inheriting an existing entity's policies (authorization binding via identity collision). Includes control login for the real privileged principal and attacker login that tries to impersonate by setting the nested claim.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: Effective permissions must not exceed upstream intent; an attacker principal must not gain privileged access by manipulating which claim is used as the identity alias (identity_claim_json_pointer confusion leading to policy inheritance).

params.description: jwt mount for identity-claim pointer confusion test

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control admin login failed or could not read admin secret; test setup invalid for authorization-binding evaluation.
Attacker obtained admin secret read via identity alias/policy inheritance (identity_claim_json_pointer confusion), exceeding upstream intent and broker policy.
Attacker could not read user secret; indicates broken baseline authorization rather than a targeted over-grant test.
Attacker and admin mapped to the same entity, enabling privilege inheritance and violating authorization binding.
